To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed a novel, high sensitive system for measuring enzyme-substrate kinetics and demonstrated its performance in measuring catalase activity, both in living cells and liver biopsies, which can be used for disease diagnosis and monitoring.
we have developed a novel, sensitive, non-invasive, and real-time measurement system for direct measurement of catalases activity in living cells, tissue biopsies, and in vivo.

the novel measurement system we developed is capable of measuring enzyme activity directly in living cells and very small amount of biological samples such as liver biopsies, which has potential applications in clinical diagnostics and intraoperative surgery.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a novel, high-sensitivity measurement system that can directly measure enzyme-substrate interactions, and hence the enzyme activity, in living cells and tissues in real-time.
the development of a novel measurement system that can directly measure catalase activity in real time.
the development of a new technology to measure the activity of enzymes in real time.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the described system has the capability to directly measure enzyme-substrate kinetics, and hence enzyme activity in living cells, in small amounts of tissue biopsies and even in clinical samples.
this system is a novel, high sensitive, non-invasive measurement tool for measuring diffusion-limit enzyme-substrate kinetics and catalase activity in real time.

this system is an important step towards the realization of the dream of a real time, high sensitivity, non-invasive, non-destructive measurement tool for measuring enzyme activity in living cells, tissues and in clinical biopsies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

this novel measurement system can be a valuable tool for measuring enzyme-substrate interactions and enzyme activities in biological specimens and can be used for diagnostic purposes in clinical settings.
this is a novel, high-sensitivity system for measuring diffusion limited enzyme-substrate kinetics and its performance is validated in living cells and small tissue biopsies.
we demonstrate the capability of our system for measuring enzyme activities in living cells and small amounts of tissue samples in real time, with high sensitivity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
our system provides an easy and robust method for measuring enzyme activity in living cells as well as in small tissue biopsies in real-time.
the proposed measurement system can be applied to a variety of enzyme-substrate pairs in living cells and biopsies.
our system can be used for measuring enzyme-substrate kinetics directly in living cells and clinical specimens in real time, and that the measured kinetics follow Michaelis-Menton reaction kinetics.
